order.A: However, in 2006, two naturalists found a tree taller than Helios. They were so overwhelmed by its height that they named it after one of the Titans from Greek myths, Hyperion. Hyperion was the name of the Titan of the Sun, meaning "the highest one."
order.B: You will have to visit Redwood National Park in the United States to find it. Redwoods are known as the tallest plants in the world. Typically, redwoods grow over 60 m, and it is easy to find them exceeding 90 m. Among them, a redwood named Hyperion stands enormously tall, reaching over 115 m. It holds the record as the world's tallest tree. Before it was discovered, Helios, which was 114 m, was considered to be the tallest tree.
order.C: However, the odds of you seeing Hyperion at the park are slim to none. The park keeps its precise location a secret to protect it from potential harm caused by visitors. The height difference between Hyperion and its neighboring redwoods is merely a few meters, making it nearly impossible to identify from the ground. Every redwood in the park will look like a giant from the bottom.

read.ko: eucalyptus가 그러한 예입니다.
read.en: Eucalyptus is one such example.

read.ko: eucalyptus 씨앗은 모래 알갱이만큼 작지만, 그것들은 단단한 캡슐 안에 함께 묶여 있습니다.
read.en: Eucalyptus seeds are as tiny as grains of sand, but they are bound together in firm capsules.

read.ko: 그것들이 강한 껍질로 단단히 보호되어 있기 때문에 새들은 그것들을 먹을 수 없습니다.
read.en: Birds cannot eat them because they are securely protected by a strong shell.

read.ko: 덥고 건조한 날씨가 길게 이어지는 시기에, 이 잎들은 인화성이 매우 높은 기름을 포함하고 있기 때문에 eucalyptus 잎들은 서로 마찰하면서 자연적으로 불이 붙습니다.
read.en: In long periods of hot and dry weather, eucalyptus leaves rub together and naturally catch fire because the leaves contain highly flammable oil.

read.ko: 불에서 발생한 극심한 열기는 껍질이 갈라져 열리게 합니다.
read.en: The extreme heat from the fire causes the shell to crack open.

read.ko: 마침내, 씨앗들이 껍질에서 나와, 땅에 떨어지고, 자라기 시작합니다.
read.en: Finally, the seeds come out of the shell, hit the ground, and begin to grow.

read.ko: 떨어진 씨앗들은 화재 후 편리하게도 남은 부드러운 재 속에 감춰지는데, 이것은 그것들을 가혹한 환경으로부터 보호합니다.
read.en: The fallen seeds are conveniently concealed in the soft ash left over after the fire, which protects them from the harsh environment.

read.ko: 종종 모체 나무에 의해 시작되는 산불은 또한 지상의 거의 모든 것을 태워, 성장에 필요한 물과 햇빛을 위해 씨앗들과 경쟁할 다른 식물들을 파괴합니다.
read.en: Wildfire, often started by the parent tree, also burns practically everything on the ground, destroying other plants that would compete with the seeds for the water and sunlight needed for growth.

read.ko: 보시다시피, eucalyptus는 화재가 있을 경우에만 번식할 수 있습니다.
read.en: As you can see, eucalyptus is only able to reproduce provided that there is fire.

read.ko: 세계에서 가장 높은 나무는 어디서 찾을 수 있을까요?
read.en: Where would you find the tallest tree in the world?

read.ko: 여러분은 그것을 찾기 위해 미국의 Redwood 국립공원을 방문해야 할 것입니다.
read.en: You will have to visit Redwood National Park in the United States to find it.

read.ko: redwood는 세계에서 가장 높은 식물로 알려져 있습니다.
read.en: Redwoods are known as the tallest plants in the world.

read.ko: 일반적으로, redwood는 60m 이상 자라며, 그것이 90 m를 초과하는 것을 발견하는 것은 쉽습니다.
read.en: Typically, redwoods grow over 60 m, and it is easy to find them exceeding 90 m.

read.ko: 그들 중에서, Hyperion이라고 불리는 redwood는 엄청나게 높이 서 있으며, 115m 이상에 달합니다.
read.en: Among them, a redwood named Hyperion stands enormously tall, reaching over 115 m.

read.ko: 그것은 세계에서 가장 높은 나무로서 기록을 보유하고 있습니다.
read.en: It holds the record as the world's tallest tree.

read.ko: 그것이 발견되기 전에는, 114m였던 Helios가 가장 높은 나무로 여겨졌습니다.
read.en: Before it was discovered, Helios, which was 114 m, was considered to be the tallest tree.

read.ko: 하지만, 2006년에, 두 명의 자연학자가 Helios보다 더 높은 나무를 발견했습니다.
read.en: However, in 2006, two naturalists found a tree taller than Helios.

read.ko: 그들은 그 나무의 높이에 매우 압도되어서 그 나무를 그리스 신화의 Titan 중 하나인 Hyperion으로 이름 지었습니다.
read.en: They were so overwhelmed by its height that they named it after one of the Titans from Greek myths, Hyperion.

read.ko: Hyperion은 태양의 Tatan의 이름이었고, ‘가장 높은 자'를 의미합니다.
read.en: Hyperion was the name of the Titan of the Sun, meaning "the highest one."

read.ko: 하지만, 여러분이 공원에서 Hyperion을 볼 가능성은 희박합니다.
read.en: However, the odds of you seeing Hyperion at the park are slim to none.

read.ko: 공원은 나무를 방문객들에 의해 발생되는 잠재적 피해로부터 보호하기 위해 나무의 정확한 위치를 비밀로 유지합니다.
read.en: The park keeps its precise location a secret to protect it from potential harm caused by visitors.

read.ko: 여러분은 redwood 사이에서 그것을 쉽게 찾을 수 있다고 생각할 수 있지만, 그것은 여러분이 생각하는 것보다 더 어렵습니다.
read.en: You may assume you can easily find it among the redwoods, but it is harder than you think.

read.ko: Hyperion과 인접한 redwood 간의 높이 차이는 단지 몇 미터에 불과해서, 지상에서 식별하는 것을 거의 불가능하게 만듭니다.
read.en: The height difference between Hyperion and its neighboring redwoods is merely a few meters, making it nearly impossible to identify from the ground.

read.ko: 공원에 있는 모든 redwood는 아래에서 보면 거인처럼 보일 것입니다.
read.en: Every redwood in the park will look like a giant from the bottom.

para.en: Plants are amazing. Throughout their long existence, they have created diverse survival strategies. Seeds, in particular, are one of the strongest survival techniques they have developed. Let's discover the fascinating and mysterious world of seeds.

Plants will do anything to spread their seeds. They offer tasty food to animals in return for distributing their seeds. Jackfruit, the world's largest tree fruit, has a sweet smell that attracts animals, similar to pineapples and bananas. It tempts animals to eat delicious fruit flesh, thereby getting them to eat the seeds. The fruit flesh is digested by the animals that consume it, but the seeds are not digested and pass through the animals' digestive tracts untouched. When these animals poop out the seeds, the seeds begin to sprout and grow, and jackfruit spreads. In exchange for a satisfying meal, the animals spread the jackfruit seeds.

Many plants opt to scatter their seeds by providing food to animals, but not all of them do. Some plants attach their seeds to passing animals, spreading them without any return benefit. Instead of tempting sweet fruits, these seeds are equipped with sharp hooks or needles. Devil's claw stands out as the most vicious of these plants. Devil's claw primarily inhabits the Kalahari Desert in South Africa, Namibia, and Botswana. Its blossoms resembling pink trumpets eventually transform into fruits with many hooks. As these fruits dry, they become solid, and their hooks become tough enough to attach to the bodies of animals. As animals pass by, the hooks extending in all directions will keep the dried fruit firmly attached to their fur. As the animals move away, the seeds from the fruit will be scattered in various locations. The attached hooks cause severe pain to the animals, making them feel like the devil is scratching them with its horrifying claws. That is how devil's claw became known as the worst free rider. 113 2

Out of numerous creative methods for spreading seeds, silver arrow-reed in South Africa has a particularly unique one. Silver arrow-reed spreads its seeds by deceiving dung beetles. Dung beetles, by nature, roll antelope dung and bury it in the ground to eat or lay eggs in. Silver arrow-reed seeds are dark brown, round, and slightly larger than 1 cm in size. Their visual appearance and smell are quite similar to antelope dung. So when a seed falls onto the ground, dung beetles will approach the fallen seed within minutes. Then, they carefully roll the seed away as if it were antelope dung. That is why dung beetles are often spotted rolling silver arrow-reed seeds that look and smell like dung balls. When they try to eat the seeds or lay eggs inside of them, however, the confused beetles will realize they cannot. They have no choice but to abort and search for real dung balls. By tricking dung beetles to roll away and bury the seeds, silver arrow-reed is able to spread and plant its seeds better.

Not all seeds are transported by animals. Some are carried by the wind. This approach is used by maple trees. Maple seeds are shaped like a boomerang with irregular ridges on the surface. When a maple seed falls from the tree, it spins around. This rotation makes the seed stay in the air longer and fly farther. It is similar to how helicopters get lifted and stay in the air using their propellers. The rotation caused by its wings allows the maple seed to elevate twice as high as non-rotating seeds. As a result, it can travel much farther from the parent tree. The rotation also slows down the speed of the fall, and the seed softly lands on the ground. This helps reduce the damage to the seed during the fall. 114 3

In most cases, mature seeds are automatically separated from the parent plant. However, some plants only release their seeds after enduring an extreme experience. Eucalyptus is one such example. Eucalyptus seeds are as tiny as grains of sand, but they are bound together in firm capsules. Birds cannot eat them because they are securely protected by a strong shell. In long periods of hot and dry weather, eucalyptus leaves rub together and naturally catch fire because the leaves contain highly flammable oil. The extreme heat from the fire causes the shell to crack open. Finally, the seeds come out of the shell, hit the ground, and begin to grow. The fallen seeds are conveniently concealed in the soft ash left over after the fire, which protects them from the harsh environment. Wildfire, often started by the parent tree, also burns practically everything on the ground, destroying other plants that would compete with the seeds for the water and sunlight needed for growth. As you can see, eucalyptus is only able to reproduce provided that there is fire.

Where would you find the tallest tree in the world? You will have to visit Redwood National Park in the United States to find it. Redwoods are known as the tallest plants in the world. Typically, redwoods grow over 60 m, and it is easy to find them exceeding 90 m. Among them, a redwood named Hyperion stands enormously tall, reaching over 115 m. It holds the record as the world's tallest tree. Before it was discovered, Helios, which was 114 m, was considered to be the tallest tree. However, in 2006, two naturalists found a tree taller than Helios. They were so overwhelmed by its height that they named it after one of the Titans from Greek myths, Hyperion. Hyperion was the name of the Titan of the Sun, meaning "the highest one." However, the odds of you seeing Hyperion at the park are slim to none. The park keeps its precise location a secret to protect it from potential harm caused by visitors. You may assume you can easily find it among the redwoods, but it is harder than you think. The height difference between Hyperion and its neighboring redwoods is merely a few meters, making it nearly impossible to identify from the ground. Every redwood in the park will look like a giant from the bottom.
